title: Unresolved alias conflicts for one run (v1)
description: runs/<run_id>/alias_conflicts.json. Contradictory alias evidence, RECORDED AND NEVER RESOLVED: both records survive unchanged, no identity moves, nothing is deleted. Resolution needs an explicit operator decision or a configured domain_migration rule, neither of which is this artifact's business. The envelope is validated too, not just the entries, so a document with a count that disagrees with its own rows cannot be written.

alias_conflicts_count.description: DERIVED from `conflicts`, never supplied by a caller. Present so the manifest can report the count without re-reading this file, and asserted equal to the row count by the builder before a byte is written.

conflicts.description: Sorted deterministically by (reason, identity_url, proposed_alias) so two runs over one input produce byte-identical output. An empty array is a real, valid answer: a run that found no contradictory evidence says so rather than omitting the artifact.

conflict_id.description: sha256 of (reason, identity_url, proposed_alias), first 16 hex. Content-derived, so the same contradiction gets the same id in every run and an id cannot depend on iteration order.

reason.description: The committed S6-3 vocabulary. Deliberately NOT record.v1.json's rejection_reason enum: a conflict rejects nothing, it declines to alias and says why.

identity_url.description: The record whose alias was proposed. Read for attribution only — a conflict never moves an identity.

proposed_alias.description: The alias that was refused, or null when the evidence was too malformed to name one.

resolution.description: Always unresolved in this artifact. A resolved conflict is not a conflict, and nothing in Stage 6 resolves one.
